Furthermore, I also have in mind the statement given by General Nicolai, the UNPROFOR commander, which he gave in 1996 and in this statement he said that he had ordered the commander of the DutchBat, Colonel Karremans, at the meeting with General Mladic on the evening of the 11th, that he requested him, or rather, the army to allow the population to leave the territory under the control of the BH army. Also, I had in mind the first sentence uttered by Mr. Mladic at the meeting with Karremans in Bratunac. He said, "What do you want?" Which means that this was not his initiative but rather the initiative of the United Nations whose representative was Lieutenant-Colonel Karremans. So all this information is something that convinced me that this was not a forcible expulsion but that it was, rather, based on expressed will. But what was this will and desire based upon? As a rule, when an army leaves an area, the civilian population follows in their suit and they join the army. This is a rule that pertains to every conflict, particularly civil wars, because the population wants to go to the same territory where their army is going. However, this decision was not made by the VRS but rather by UNPROFOR in agreement with the civilian authorities of Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you find a single document purported to say that I ordered illegal actions to be taken against the prisoners of war in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't find any such information. In the two orders that we spoke about, you explicitly said that they must be treated in a lawful manner.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you find any document in which I was informed by anyone about unlawful treatment of prisoners, specifically the executions of prisoners of war?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC
utterances.text: I did not find a single document of the kind. There was not even an indication that would point to that direction, especially not from you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I hope you can remember and you had an opportunity to see in the document, that in the media and in various documents there were stories about executions of men and boys. Was there any reference made to them being prisoners of war?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC
utterances.text: The media mainly reported about executions of men and boys, but it was never emphasised that those were prisoners of war. I know that not even prisoners of war can be executed because that's a crime as well. But the way in which the prisoners of war are treated in comparison to civilians is definitely a different one.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell us which localities were mentioned as execution sites?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC
utterances.text: The first mass execution took place in Kravica on the Bratunac-Konjevic Polje road.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I was referring to what the media were reporting with regard to the locations that should have attracted our attention.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC
utterances.text: There was mention that the executions took place in Srebrenica; that was not the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please now have 1D21046 which is the General's CV so that he can authenticate it for the benefit of the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: While we are waiting, General, can you tell me what kind of school you finished in 1996 -- 1968?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC
utterances.text: In 1968 I finished a school for additional training of --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat his answer slowly. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could you repeat your answer slowly this time.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In 1968 I finished the school for upgrading skill of artillery officers. All academies had advanced training which were attended between the military academy and the command staff academy in this interim and that is when I finished this course.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you please look at the left part of the screen. We translated your CV and please tell us whether it's correct and then we shall tender it into evidence.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC
utterances.text: The first part, basic education, it's not post-secondary school.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It is correct in English, it should read "high school," not "post-secondary school." Once you have finished with page 1, let's move to page 2.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC
utterances.text: This section, military posts, I was deputy of the commander --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Which line?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC
utterances.text: Third from the top of "military duties." That means that chief of department for military doctrine and army development.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. This has been recorded.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC
utterances.text: I was the chief for strategy and administration, not of strategic and administrative.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC
utterances.text: I wasn't a sergeant in 1952 but rather in 1962.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: Lieutenant.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now look at the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC
utterances.text: No, this second line, no, that wasn't me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: "Expert at the federal ministry for education"?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC
utterances.text: No, no, not me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right. Should anything else be corrected?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC
utterances.text: Published literature, it's not military bibliography, "Vojna Bibliografija." It is the bibliography of the periodical called "Vojno Delo."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right. So this is reflected in the transcript now.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC
utterances.text: There is something that needs to be corrected.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Where is that? Concept of battles in the range? You mean in the area.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. The rest is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I tender into evidence the curriculum vitae of the witness? And then the entire report as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could we see the first page? General, what does an SCG mean in terms of nationality?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I haven't seen that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It says: "Srbija i Crna gora." What does that mean?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, then when we were doing this, that was probably the name of the state. After the SFRY, Yugoslavia turned into the FRY, and then the SCG, Serbia-Montenegro, so that was the last name of this state of Serbia and Montenegro.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Any objection, Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll admit them both.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the CV 65 ter 1D21046 will be Exhibit D3863 and the expert report will be Exhibit D3864.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That means you are done with your examination-in-chief, Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Excellency. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: I just wish to make sure that when we accept the report that the paragraphs that you excluded are indeed redacted. I'm not sure whether that was done.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I take it for granted. You will -- confirmed by the Registry. We'll continue tomorrow with the Prosecution's examination -- cross-examination. Before we adjourn, Mr. Robinson, I'd like to come back to the issues raised with respect to Mr. Andric's testimony. What is it that you request as regards the issue of counsel, whether he should be allowed to be accompanied by counsel or do you wish us to assign a counsel?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: We wish you to assign a counsel. That's been the request of General Andric which we support. He does not have the funds to retain his own counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It is basically for the Registry and the Chamber sees no basis at the moment to assign counsel for him.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, Mr. President, the Registry interprets their directive on assignment of counsel to exclude assigning counsel to a witness. So unless the Chamber were to order it in the interests of justice, which you have the power to do, they will not assign counsel. So there's no -- that's why Mr. Andric -- General Andric has directed his request to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: At this moment, the Chamber is not minded to assign counsel for Mr. Andric.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Very well. We'll inform him of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. The hearing is adjourned.
